findings.detail: §7.1 states group switches (`sanitation`, `drift`, `host`, `all_controls`, `all_enforcement`, `all_baseline`) 'are authoring conveniences… expanded… to explicit leaves… they are not persisted precedence layers,' explicitly 'to prevent a parent and child from prescribing incompatible outcomes.' §7.2 then persists `controls.enabled` and `enforcement.enabled` and defines 'Effective state is the logical AND of the applicable global switch, group switch, leaf, and surface' — reintroducing a persisted parent that ANDs with its children and naming 'group switch' as a factor in the AND that §7.1 said was expanded away. The two clauses disagree on whether a section-level `.enabled` is a persisted precedence layer. This is reconcilable by a reader but leaves the effective-state computation — which AT-BASE-5's 'status names every disabled or unrun control' is tested against — under-specified about whether a leaf disabled via its parent is reported per-leaf or per-group.

AT-PRESENCE-1/D6 enumerate exactly three terminal states (host-native prompt, user-configured external signature, or refuse) and hold that 'an unattended key available to the agent… is not approval.' §7.4 invents a fourth path — a 'one-time downgrade ceremony' that admits an ordinary (non-FIDO, agent-readable) key as an allowed signer for the user's own target-repo policy activation. After such a downgrade, an agent that can read the key can produce a valid activation signature with no human present, which sits in direct tension with 'no presence, no activation.' Gate 2 gates the downgrade behind a FIDO-authorized ceremony and permanent status disclosure, and correctly bars it from Gate 1 integrity (D10), so it is defensible under Gate 1's 'configurability > paternalism' latitude — but it is machinery Gate 1 does not require and weakens the presence guarantee AT-PRESENCE-1 exists to make, so it should be flagged rather than absorbed silently.

AT-DIST-1 requires the install stub to fetch 'the pinned source reference.' AD-27/§11.4 default the stub to 'the latest release' (a name that resolves to whatever tag is newest at fetch time) and explicitly reject any pin/fingerprint, so two strangers running the default stub at different times receive different source. Gate 2 reinterprets 'pinned' to mean only 'not a moving branch,' and the AT-DIST-1 evidence row tests only that behavior ('Assert the stub never pipes to a shell'; branch-vs-tag), not that a fixed/immutable default reference is used. The reinterpretation is argued reasonably and Gate 1's residual notes do not demand immutability, but the default-to-latest behavior is a narrowing of Gate 1's word 'pinned' resolved in Gate 2's favor, and the primary evidence does not exercise the pinning property itself.
